column1: All around the world, nations are already preparing for, and adapting to, climate change and its impacts.
column2: 世界各国都已经在为气候变化及其影响作准备，并着手加以适应。
column3: All around the world|在世界各地

column1: Even if we stopped all CO₂ emissions tomorrow, we would continue to see the impact of the CO₂ already released since industrial times, with scientists forecasting that global warming would continue for around 40 years.
column2: 即使明天停止一切二氧化碳排放，工业时代以来已经排出的二氧化碳仍会继续产生影响。科学家预测，全球变暖还会持续约四十年。
column4: CO₂ emissions|n. 二氧化碳排放

column1: In the meantime, ice caps would continue to melt and sea levels rise.
column2: 在此期间，冰盖会继续融化，海平面也会继续上升。

column1: Some countries and regions will suffer more extreme impacts from these changes than others.
column2: 这些变化给有些国家和地区造成的影响会比其他地方更为极端。

column1: It’s in these places that innovation is thriving.
column2: 正是在这些地方，各种创新举措蓬勃兴起。

column1: In Miami Beach, Florida, USA, seawater isn’t just breaching the island city’s walls, it’s seeping up through the ground, so the only way to save the city is to lift it up above sea level.
column2: 在美国佛罗里达州迈阿密海滩市，海水不仅冲破这座岛城的防护墙，还从地下向上渗出。因此，要保住这座城市，唯一的办法就是把它抬高到海平面以上。
column8: lift it up|把它整体抬高

column1: Starting in the lowest and most vulnerable neighbourhoods, roads have been raised by as much as 61 centimetres.
column2: 抬高道路的工程从地势最低、最易受灾的社区做起，路面最多抬高了61厘米。
column7: by as much as|幅度高达

column1: The elevation work was carried out as part of Miami Beach’s ambitious but much-needed stormwater-management programme.
column2: 这项道路抬升工程是迈阿密海滩市雨洪管理计划的一部分。该计划宏大，却也是当地亟须的。
column5: as part of|作为……的一部分

column1: In addition to the road adaptations, the city has set up new pumps that can remove up to 75,000 litres of water per minute.
column2: 除了改造道路，该市还安装了新水泵，每分钟最多可排走7.5万升水。

column1: In the face of floods, climate-mitigation strategies have often been overlooked, says Yanira Pineda, a senior sustainability coordinator.
column2: 高级可持续发展协调员亚尼拉·皮内达说，面对洪水，人们常常忽略缓解气候变化的措施。

column1: She knows that they’re essential and that the job is far from over.
column2: 她知道这些措施必不可少，而且这项工作远未结束。

column1: ‘We know that in 20, 30, 40 years, we’ll need to go back in there and adjust to the changing environment,’ she says.
column2: 她说：“我们知道，二十年、三十年、四十年后，我们需要再回到那里，适应不断变化的环境。”
column3: in 20, 30, 40 years|二十年、三十年、四十年后
column6: changing environment|n. 不断变化的环境

column1: Seawalls are a staple strategy for many coastal communities, but on the soft, muddy northern shores of Java, Indonesia, they frequently collapse, further exacerbating coastal erosion.
column2: 对许多沿海社区来说，修海堤是常用的应对办法，但在印度尼西亚爪哇岛北部松软泥泞的岸边，海堤常常坍塌，进一步加剧海岸侵蚀。

column1: There have been many attempts to restore the island’s coastal mangroves: ecosystems of trees and shrubs that help defend coastal areas by trapping sediment in their net-like root systems, elevating the sea bed and dampening the energy of waves and tidal currents.
column2: 人们曾多次试图恢复岛上的沿海红树林。红树林是由乔木和灌木构成的生态系统，有助于保护沿海地区：网状根系能截留沉积物、抬高海床，还能削弱波浪和潮流的能量。

column1: But Susanna Tol of the not-for-profit organisation Wetlands International says that, while hugely popular, the majority of mangrove-planting projects fail.
column2: 不过，非营利组织“湿地国际”的苏珊娜·托尔说，种植红树林的项目虽然极受欢迎，大部分却以失败告终。

column1: So, Wetlands International started out with a different approach, building semi-permeable dams, made from bamboo poles and brushwood, to mimic the role of mangrove roots and create favourable conditions for mangroves to grow back naturally.
column2: 于是，湿地国际一开始就采取了不同的办法，用竹竿和树枝搭建半透水坝，模拟红树林根系的作用，为红树林自然重新生长创造有利条件。

column1: The programme has seen moderate success, mainly in areas with less subsidence.
column2: 这项计划取得了一定成效，主要体现在地面沉降较轻的地区。

column1: ‘Unfortunately, traditional infrastructure is often single-solution focused,’ says Tol.
column2: 托尔说：“遗憾的是，传统的基础设施往往只着眼于解决单一问题。”
column6: single-solution focused|只着眼于单一解决办法的

column1: ‘For long-term success, it’s critical that we transition towards multifunctional approaches that embed natural processes and that engage and benefit communities and local decision-makers.’
column2: “要取得长远成效，关键是转向能发挥多种作用的做法：把自然过程融入其中，让社区和地方决策者参与，也让他们从中受益。”
column6: multifunctional approaches|n. 能发挥多种作用的做法

column1: As the floodwaters rose in the rice fields of the Mekong Delta in September 2018, four small houses rose with them.
column2: 2018年9月，随着湄公河三角洲稻田里的洪水水位上涨，四所小房子也跟着升了起来。
column6: Mekong Delta|n. 湄公河三角洲

column1: Homes in this part of Vietnam are traditionally built on stilts but these ones had been built to float.
column2: 越南这一带的传统房屋建在高桩上，而这几所房子则是按能够浮起来的方式建造的。

column1: The modifications were made by the Buoyant Foundation Project, a not-for-profit organisation that has been researching and retrofitting amphibious houses since 2006.
column2: 房屋改造由非营利组织“浮式地基项目”实施，该组织从2006年起就一直在研究和改装水陆两栖房屋。
column9: amphibious houses|n. 水陆两栖房屋

column1: ‘When I started this,’ explains founder Elizabeth English, ‘climate change was not on the tip of everybody’s tongue, but this technology is becoming necessary in places that didn’t previously need it.’
column2: 创办人伊丽莎白·英格利什解释说：“我刚开始做这件事时，人们还没有把气候变化挂在嘴边，但现在，一些从前用不着这项技术的地方也开始需要它了。”
column5: on the tip of everybody’s tongue|人人都在谈论

column1: It’s much cheaper than permanently elevating houses, English explains – about a third of what it would cost to completely replace a building’s foundations.
column2: 英格利什解释说，这比永久性抬高房屋要便宜得多，花费约为彻底更换一栋建筑地基所需费用的三分之一。

column1: It also avoids the problem of taller houses being at greater risk from wind damage.
column2: 这种做法也避开了另一个问题：房屋抬高后，遭受风损的风险会更大。
column5: at greater risk|面临更大的风险
column6: wind damage|n. 风造成的损坏

column1: Another plus comes from the fact that amphibious structures can be sensitively adapted to meet cultural needs and match the kind of houses that are already common in a community.
column2: 这种做法还有一个好处：两栖建筑可以经过细致调整，既满足当地文化需求，也与社区已有的常见房型相协调。
column4: amphibious structures|n. 水陆两栖建筑
column7: meet cultural needs|满足文化需求

column1: Bangladesh is especially vulnerable to climate change.
column2: 孟加拉国尤其容易受到气候变化的影响。

column1: Most of the country is less than a metre above sea level and 80 per cent of its land lies on floodplains.
column2: 该国大部分地区海拔不足一米，80%的国土位于洪泛平原上。

column1: ‘Almost 35 million people living on the coastal belt of Bangladesh are currently affected by soil and water salinity,’ says Raisa Chowdhury of the international development organisation ICCO Cooperation.
column2: 国际发展组织ICCO Cooperation的赖萨·乔杜里说：“目前，居住在孟加拉国沿海地带的近3500万人正受到土壤和水体含盐问题的影响。”
column7: soil and water salinity|n. 土壤和水体的含盐量

column1: Rather than fighting against it, one project is helping communities adapt to salt-affected soils.
column2: 有一个项目换了种应对方式：帮助社区适应受盐分影响的土壤，而不是试图与盐分对抗。
column7: salt-affected soils|n. 受盐分影响的土壤

column1: ICCO Cooperation has been working with 10,000 farmers in Bangladesh to start cultivating naturally salt-tolerant crops in the region.
column2: ICCO Cooperation一直在与孟加拉国的一万名农民合作，着手在当地种植天然耐盐的作物。

column1: Certain varieties of carrot, potato, kohlrabi, cabbage and beetroot have been found to be better suited to salty soil than the rice and wheat that is typically grown there.
column2: 人们发现，某些品种的胡萝卜、马铃薯、球茎甘蓝、卷心菜和甜菜根，比当地通常种植的水稻和小麦更适合盐分较高的土壤。

column1: Chowdhury says that the results are very visible, comparing a barren plot of land to the ‘beautiful, lush green vegetable garden’ sitting beside it, in which he and his team have been working with the farmers.
column2: 乔杜里说，成效一目了然。他把一块荒地和旁边那片“漂亮、郁郁葱葱的菜园”作了对比，他和团队正是在这片菜园里与农民一起工作。

column1: Since the project began, farmers trained in saline agriculture have reported increases of two to three more harvests per year.
column2: 自项目启动以来，接受过盐土农业培训的农民表示，他们每年能比过去多收获两到三季。

column1: Greg Spotts from Los Angeles (LA) in the USA is chief sustainability officer of the city’s street services department.
column2: 美国洛杉矶市的格雷格·斯波茨是该市街道服务部门的首席可持续发展官。

column1: He leads the Cool Streets LA programme, a series of pilot projects, which include the planting of trees and the installation of a ‘cool pavement’ system, designed to help reach the city’s goal of bringing down its average temperature by 1.5°C.
column2: 他领导的“洛杉矶清凉街道”计划包含一系列试点项目，其中有植树和安装“降温路面”系统，目的是帮助这座城市实现平均气温降低1.5摄氏度的目标。
column9: reach the city’s goal|实现市政府的目标

column1: ‘Urban cooling is literally a matter of life and death for our future in LA,’ says Spotts.
column2: 斯波茨说：“就洛杉矶的未来而言，城市降温确确实实是生死攸关的事。”
column5: a matter of life and death|生死攸关的事

column1: Using a Geographic Information System data mapping tool, the programme identified streets with low tree canopy cover in three of the city’s neighbourhoods and covered them with a light-grey, light-reflecting coating, which had already been shown to lower road surface temperature in Los Angeles by 6°C.
column2: 项目团队利用地理信息系统的数据制图工具，在市内三个社区找出树冠覆盖率低的街道，并在这些街道上铺设了浅灰色的反光涂层。此前已经证实，这种涂层能使洛杉矶的路表温度降低6摄氏度。
column3: Geographic Information System|n. 地理信息系统
column6: tree canopy cover|n. 树冠覆盖率
column10: road surface temperature|n. 路表温度

column1: Spotts says one of these streets, in the Winnetka neighbourhood of San Fernando Valley, can now be seen as a pale crescent, the only cool spot on an otherwise red thermal image, from the International Space Station.
column2: 斯波茨说，其中一条街道位于圣费尔南多谷的温内特卡社区，如今看起来像一弯浅色的新月，从国际空间站看去，它是热成像图上唯一一处凉点，周围全是红色。
column6: cool spot|n. 温度较低的一处
column9: International Space Station|n. 国际空间站
